run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-15T09:53:17Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate warning for otel-demo/frontend-proxy is driven by 504 gateway timeouts (Envoy 'UT response_timeout' at ~15000 ms) that occur only on the /api/recommendations route. Observed chain: load-generator GET -> frontend-proxy 'ingress' span with error=true, http.status_code=504 at ~15.0s -> frontend-proxy 'router frontend egress' error at 15.0s -> frontend 'GET /api/recommendations' returning 200 after 19.06s -> frontend client span grpc.oteldemo.RecommendationService/ListRecommendations at 19.06s. Frontend p90 for GET /api/recommendations rose from ~200ms to 8.3s (09:51) and 14.1s (09:56) while every other frontend route stayed at 60-105ms, so the degradation is scoped to the recommendation path. The deepest cause the evidence supports is the single recommendation pod being CPU-saturated at its 100m limit: container CPU usage rose from 0.0124 to 0.0959 cores and CFS throttling from ~5% to 97-100% from 09:47-09:52, the highest throttle ratio among the 21 otel-demo pods, with request volume flat and no restart, OOM or memory-limit pressure. That inflation pushes recommendation's gRPC responses past frontend-proxy's 15s upstream timeout, producing the 504s that raise frontend-proxy's error rate above 0. What raised recommendation's per-request CPU demand at ~09:46 is not determinable from the available data. A separate fraud-detection OOMKilled/restart event is not on this path and is not the cause.

claims.text: frontend-proxy's error spans are exclusively operation 'ingress' with status tags error=true, http.status_code=504, otel.status_code=ERROR, each ~15.0s long (15000351-15001257 us); their 13m increase climbs from ~1.15 at 09:33:17 to 58.54 at 10:02:27 on span 'ingress', while 'router frontend egress' error stays 0 in the same metric.

frontend-proxy's own access log shows the failing requests as 504 with Envoy response timeout: lines 'GET /api/recommendations?productIds=... HTTP/1.1" 504 UT response_timeout ... 15000/15001 ms' timestamped 09:54:55 through 09:58:41; every line matching a 504 in that window is /api/recommendations, with client python-requests/2.32.5.

One complete trace (57088b67f3666e7e4a384456d6806abd, 09:58:46) shows the failure topology with parent references: load-generator 'GET' 15.00s error=true http.status_code=504 -> frontend-proxy 'ingress' 15.00s error=true http.status_code=504 -> frontend-proxy 'router frontend egress' 15.00s (error="true", http.status_code="0") -> frontend 'GET /api/recommendations' 19.06s http.status_code=200 -> frontend 'grpc.oteldemo.RecommendationService/ListRecommendations' 19.06s rpc.grpc.status_code=0. The trace contains no recommendation-service span.

Frontend p90 by span shows the degradation confined to the recommendation path: 'GET /api/recommendations' 246ms (09:31) -> 8271ms (09:51) -> 14129ms (09:56), and client span 'grpc.oteldemo.RecommendationService/ListRecommendations' 120ms -> 8246ms -> 13912ms, while 'GET /api/cart' (74-126ms), 'GET /api/products/{productId}' (65-81ms), 'POST /api/checkout' (391-611ms), 'GET /api/data' (61-110ms) and 'grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds' (55-98ms) stay flat over the same window.

The recommendation pod's container CPU usage rises from 0.0124 cores (steady 09:31-09:47) to 0.0959 cores by 09:51:57 and then stays at ~0.0955-0.0962, i.e. pinned at the deployment's 100m CPU limit (limits cpu=100m, requests cpu=30m, replicas 1).

The recommendation pod's CFS throttled-periods ratio rises from ~0.05 to 0.306 (09:47:57), 0.516, 0.699, 0.856, 0.970 and then holds 0.964-1.0 until the end of the window; in the final 13m comparison it is 0.698, the highest of all 21 otel-demo pods (frontend 0.225, frontend-proxy 0.038, product-catalog 0.190, cart 0.225).

Request volume to the recommendation path is flat while recommendation's CPU rises: frontend 'GET /api/recommendations' increases stay 213.9-310 per 5m across the whole window (e.g. 236.7 at 09:52:17, 246.7 at 09:57:17), and recommendation's log line rate is ~1.1 'Receive ListRecommendations' lines/second at 09:46 and ~0.7/second at 09:57.

The recommendation pod shows no restart, OOM or memory-limit pressure: phase Running, ready true, restartCount 0, container started 2026-11-15T09:11:56Z, and working-set memory moves only from 41.9MB to a fluctuating 44-60MB against a 160Mi limit.

recommendation's own client-side latency grows too: p90 of '/oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/ListProducts' and of internal 'get_product_list' rise from 9.5-15.8ms (09:33-09:40) to 320ms (09:52:17) and 833ms (09:53:17), while product-catalog's server spans visible in the sampled trace are 29-149us with rpc.grpc.status_code=0.

recommendation's own span export stops during the worst period: per-5m increase of '/oteldemo.RecommendationService/ListRecommendations', 'get_product_list' and '/oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/ListProducts' falls from 310 (09:39:17) to 142.2, 86.7, 27.8 and then 0 from 09:55:17 onward, and their p90 becomes NaN from 09:57:37, even though the pod keeps logging 'Receive ListRecommendations' until at least 09:58:21.

Error spans by service show frontend-proxy alone climbing (0 -> 58.5 per 13m at 10:02), while frontend, cart and payment stay at 0 throughout, ad holds a flat ~1.04, recommendation holds ~1.04-2.08 from 09:36 to 09:52 then 0 from 09:57, and fraud-detection moves 0 -> ~1.03 from 09:53. Separately, recommendation's flagd client span '/flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream' recorded two error spans with rpc.grpc.status_code=4 (DEADLINE_EXCEEDED, 600.004s) at 09:23:46 and 09:33:46.

frontend-proxy itself is not resource-constrained: its CPU throttled-periods ratio is 0.028-0.047 across the window and its working set is a steady ~20.3-20.7MB against a 50Mi limit; its ingress p90 nevertheless rises from ~186-290ms (09:35-09:47) to 850-1156ms (09:55-10:05) because it holds timed-out upstream connections.

fraud-detection changed during the window for its own separate reason: its container's last termination was reason OOMKilled with exitCode 137, restartCount 3, current container started 2026-11-15T09:33:20Z; its throttle ratio was 1.0 until ~09:34 and dropped to 0.008-0.09 afterwards, and its working set is ~331-334MB.

Primary explanation: frontend-proxy's 504s are caused by the recommendation pod's CPU starvation. The sequence is recommendation CPU usage ramping at 09:47-09:52 to its 100m limit with 97-100% CFS throttling, frontend's p90 for the recommendation call jumping from ~200ms to 8.3-14.1s at 09:51-09:56, and frontend-proxy returning 504 UT response_timeout at its 15s Envoy upstream timeout from ~09:54. The ordering (CPU throttle onset precedes the latency and error ramp) and the mechanism (a throttled single-replica gRPC server cannot answer within 15s) are consistent, but the step from CPU throttling to a 15s response is inferred from correlation of these series, not measured end-to-end.

Secondary, unverified hypothesis for why recommendation's per-request CPU demand rose roughly 8x while request volume stayed flat: its flagd feature-flag stream. recommendation's '/flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream' client span recorded DEADLINE_EXCEEDED (grpc status 4) at 09:23:46 and 09:33:46, its EventStream spans appear only until ~09:43 and its per-5m EventStream count is 0 after 09:47, immediately before or alongside the CPU ramp; a broken or retrying flag stream could burn CPU. This cannot be confirmed: the flagd pod produced no readable log lines in this Run.

recommendation is not failing in the error sense: it registers 0 error spans from 09:57 onward, keeps a restartCount of 0 with the same container instance started at 09:11:56Z, and its application log continues receiving 'Receive ListRecommendations' calls at ~0.7/second through 09:58:21. Its contribution to the alert is latency and CPU starvation, not request errors. (Whether it logged any error text was not established; the filtered log view for that returned no_data.)

frontend is not itself erroring: it has 0 error spans over the window and returned http.status_code=200 on GET /api/recommendations even at 19.06s duration; its CPU throttling (0.21-0.27) and memory (~122-132MB of 200Mi) are unchanged from the start of the window. The 504 is generated by frontend-proxy's 15s upstream timeout, not by a frontend failure.

Rejected as the cause of this alert: fraud-detection's OOMKill and 3 restarts. fraud-detection is not on the traced failing path (the 504 chain is frontend-proxy -> frontend -> recommendation), its container restart at 09:33:20 precedes the 09:53 error ramp by about 20 minutes, and its throttling fell from 1.0 to ~0.04 after that restart rather than rising. Its ~1 error span per 13m from 09:53 is a separate, low-volume signal.

Rejected as the cause: a traffic spike or a downstream product-catalog fault. Frontend 'GET /api/recommendations' volume is flat at ~214-310 spans per 5m across the window while recommendation's CPU rises 8x, and product-catalog's own server spans stayed 29-149us with rpc.grpc.status_code=0 while recommendation's client-side call to it slowed to 833ms p90.

Raise the recommendation deployment's CPU limit (currently limits.cpu=100m, requests.cpu=30m, replicas=1) or add replicas so the single throttled pod is not the throughput ceiling; the pod is consuming its full 100m quota with 97-100% of CFS periods throttled.

Profile the recommendation container to identify what raised per-request CPU at ~09:46 (request volume was flat), and review its OpenFeature/flagd client behaviour given the DEADLINE_EXCEEDED EventStream spans; compare against change history for this deployment, which is not integrated in this Run.

gaps: What raised the recommendation pod's CPU demand about 8x at ~09:46 while request volume stayed flat is unknown; there is no change-history integration and no log, event or configuration evidence of a trigger.

The recommendation service's own server-side latency during 09:54-10:06 is unknown: its span export stopped (calls_total for all its operations 0 from 09:55:17, p90 NaN from 09:57:37) even though it kept logging requests, so its internal view of the slow calls is a telemetry gap.

The alert's own expression and value could not be reproduced: list_prometheus_rules returned no_data for rule_name RequestErrorRate (status no_data), and no http_server_request_duration_seconds_count series exist in this window (status no_data). The spans-based error ratio for frontend-proxy peaked around 0.0136 at 09:56, not the 0.0667 stated in the annotation, so the metric and window behind the annotation are unverified.

Whether recommendation logged any error text is unconfirmed: the filtered log query over 09:40-09:58 returned no_data (910 lines read, 0 matched), so absence of error lines is a limit of that view, not evidence of health.

flagd's logs were unavailable: the log query for pod flagd-785747d9d9-zsjrc returned no_data with 0 lines read for all three containers, so the flag-stream hypothesis could be neither verified nor refuted.

Node-level CPU and memory metrics are unavailable: the query for node_cpu*/node_load* returned no_data, so CPU contention from co-located pods on node i-07fdfccf76e0651ab (also hosting recommendation and frontend-proxy) could not be ruled out.
No pre-incident baseline exists for these series: the earlier window 07:00-07:53 returned no_data, and all series start around 09:28-09:29, so all comparisons are within the incident window only.

Two log views were incomplete by row limit (9835e9e6-7d7c-4f40-a598-aa8b646bcfbb-t1:8c8bfae5-128b-40c8-929c-eb215f7a74ce; a17301a2-7443-48cc-8773-ef70d170b372-t1:da844b9a-b233-4756-b770-c27f48ae4ce7; d8b23db4-e9c0-4cd2-a1d9-771e0a67661e-t0:fb2ca7d2-4ef5-498a-8dc2-aedde6d30d43; 30bf2a7e-366e-48b2-9266-79bdc2d0194f-t1:424fc602-025f-4d00-ac81-c5efbcbcd22b) and one hit the 4 MiB read limit (d36c0b2e-4153-40fa-8747-3b364dc1b247-t0:9f881d27-9fc9-4753-adbe-5f8d5ccb080e), so lines beyond those cuts remain unknown.
Impact beyond the demo path (customer-facing consequences) was not observed and is unverified; only the demo services' own spans, logs and container metrics were measured.
next_steps: Compare recommendation's CPU profile and configuration/flag-provider settings before and after ~09:46 using the change-history integration, which is not available here.
Inspect recommendation's OTel span-export pipeline state to explain why its spans stopped being exported from ~09:55, since that hides its server-side latency.

Confirm frontend-proxy's Envoy response_timeout setting (evidenced as 15000 ms on the 504 lines) is intended for the /api/recommendations route and whether a shorter fail-fast or retry policy is preferable.
Check node i-07fdfccf76e0651ab's CPU saturation for the incident period using node-exporter data, which was unavailable in this Run.
Retrieve the actual RequestErrorRate alerting rule definition from Prometheus/Alertmanager configuration to reconcile the reported 0.0667 error rate with the observed 504 counts.
